first.rationale: Prioritize onboarding simplification because completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates durable activation and time-to-value gains from reducing onboarding friction. Verify the onboarding result and the promotional-pricing retention downside before committing, since competitor pricing creates pressure but retention harm would conflict with sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. Completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, while the verified onboarding result improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%. Promotional pricing addresses competitive pressure but its verified 12% retention decline and failure to survive first renewal make it unsuitable for the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. The precise source of the current declines remains uncertain, so measure completion, first meaningful action, qualified conversion, and retention by segment.

final2.rationale: Keep the onboarding-simplification experiment. The deeper price cut and doubled churn conversations increase urgency, but verified promotional pricing drove a 12% 30-day retention decline and failed to survive first renewal, directly undermining sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Simplified onboarding has confirmed benefits to completion, time-to-value, activation, and 30-day retention, while addressing the current declines in onboarding completion and activation. Monitor price-sensitive SMB churn separately; this experiment is not assumed to resolve price-driven churn.
